newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unions call for widespread oil disruption.
newsitem.headline: French unions call for widespread oil disruption.

text.p: French unions on Friday called for disruption at refineries across the country to protest about pay, retirment age and job cuts.
A joint statement by five unions said they would consult their branches on the type of action to take in the hope of expanding a spate of isolated protests to include all plants.

The appeal came as oil firms began to recover from a crippling 12-day refinery blockade by French truckers and Elf Aquitaine workers extended a two-day forced shutdown of three Elf refineries by another 24 hours.
"Oil company staff are counting on getting (oil industry association) UFIP and the oil firms to negotiate ways of boosting employment," the statement by the CFDT, CGC, CFTC, CGT and FO unions said.
It said the unions wanted oil companies to cancel plans to cut jobs in a shake-up of the refining sector, improve an offer to increase pay by 1.3 percent and allow retirement at 55.

Esso France earlier on Friday announced plans to shed 10 percent of its workforce over two years and Elf Aquitaine workers extended a refinery strike over similar plans at distribution subsidiary Elf Antar.

Retirement at 55 instead of 60 was a key concession won by truck drivers in their strike which ended on Friday. The strike brought fuel shortages and rationing in many areas after truckers blocked the exits of all French refineries. Oil firms said they would race to deliver petrol over the weekend.
